newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA WHEEL OUT FORMULA ONE CHALLENGER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA WHEEL OUT FORMULA ONE CHALLENGER.

text.p: The new Lola Formula One team introduced their 1997 world championship challenger on Thursday.
Team founder Eric Broadley said of his fledgling outfit: "We are completely ready for this venture.
"Like all projects the eventual aim is to win the championship and, after four years, I am expecting us to do that.
"I am not predicting big results this year, we have a lot to learn and there are a lot of other good teams out there, but we will win in the future."
Broadley made it clear that the team would not achieve that kind of success until they replace their current Ford engines with their own Lola power-unit, which is already near completion.
"We are not going to win in Formula One without a super engine and the view was that if we couldn't get it, then we would have to make one," he added.
"I have no fears at the moment. We should get within the 107 percent qualifying minimum and if we don't do that then we should not be in the sport."
The driver line-up has already been confirmed as Italian Vincenzo Sospiri and Brazilian Ricardo Rosset. Italian Andrea Montermini has signed as test driver.

"This is my first year in the sport and I am looking forward to it," said Sospiri. "I hope we can just get points before the end of the year and I am sure we will have no problems qualifying throughout the season."
The Lola T97/30 will be tested for the first time at Santa Pod Raceway in England on Saturday, before a major two-day run at Silverstone early next week.
The cars will be flown to Australia next Thursday ahead of the season-opening Australian Grand Prix at Melbourne on March 9.
